"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 2401: an abbreviation-period detector.

The component goes clearly negative on a full stop that closes an abbreviated word, as in
"Pat." (patent), "Col.", "Vol.", "Art.", "No.", "Fig.", "Dec." or "Aug.". It is weaker on
a full stop after a short lowercase fragment ("etc.", "vs.") and on the first token of a
document, where it is slightly negative. It is slightly positive on dotted names and URLs
such as "://" and ".org". Every other token predicts 0. Initials ("J.") and full-word
sentence ends ("...the house.") predict 0.
"""

READS = ()

ABBREVIATIONS = frozenset(
    "Pat Art Col Hon Acc Vol No Nos Fig Eq Sec Sect Ser Dept Gen Rev Ref Res Fed Hist Prof "
    "Vet App Ave Rd Rt St Ct Inc Ltd Co Jr Sr Esq Sup Doc Tex Cir Id Ed Bd "
    "Jan Feb Mar Apr Jun Jul Aug Sep Sept Oct Nov Dec".split()
)


def _word(token):
    return token.strip()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    token = tokens[-1]
    if t == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return carry, -0.2 if token.strip().isdigit() or not token.strip() else -0.1
    if token == ".":
        word = _word(tokens[-2])
        if word in ABBREVIATIONS:
            return carry, -0.6
        if word.isalpha() and word.islower() and len(word) <= 3:
            return carry, -0.07
        if word.isalpha() and word[:1].isupper() and not word.isupper() and len(word) <= 4:
            return carry, -0.3
        return carry, 0.0
    if token == "://" or (token.startswith(".") and token[1:].isalpha()):
        return carry, 0.1
    return carry, 0.0

"""Government and public-administration words, as negative activations.

This component goes strongly negative on the token that names a government or an
administration: 府 and 政府 (government: 县政府, 区政府, 当地政府), 行政 (administrative,
administration, 行政机关), 政 as a stem of policy and finance words (政策, 财政), and
Vietnamese "Chính" (Chính phủ, government). It is milder on the English word
"administrative" (as in "located in the administrative territorial entity"), and on
the court word 法院. Politics words such as 政治 stay near zero. Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

# (substring of the newest token, predicted activation); the first match wins.
RULES = (
    ("府", -4.5),     # government: 政府, 县政府, 府
    ("Chính", -4.0),  # Vietnamese government: Chính phủ
    ("行政", -2.5),   # administration: 行政, 行政机关
    ("政治", 0.0),    # politics: not the government sense
    ("政", -2.5),     # policy and finance stems: 政策, 财政, 政
    ("法院", -0.5),   # court
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    for text, value in RULES:
        if text in token:
            return carry, value
    if token == "administrative":
        return carry, -1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate rare positive spikes using recognizable text-format cues.

Detect the forum heading 'Replies Latest reply', double-equals padding after
20 base64-alphabet characters (including a digit), '>' after 20 hex characters,
and a quote/comma after padding. Unindented opening package/pragma declarations
and PHP's opening declare statement also receive positive values. These motivated
rules from large training examples; ordinary small lexical fluctuations remain
unmodeled. Otherwise predict near zero, with a negative first-token correction.
All state resets at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
BASE64 = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z0-9/+]+\Z')
HEX = re.compile(r'[A-Fa-f0-9]+\Z')
FILE_DECLARATIONS = {'package', '#pragma'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    _, forum, encoded, hexadecimal, padded, php, has_digit = (
        (doc, 0, 0, 0, False, 0, False) if first else carry
    )
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip()
    padding = text.rstrip() == '==' and encoded >= 20 and has_digit
    value = -0.002
    if first:
        value = -0.07
    if (first and text in FILE_DECLARATIONS) or (
        php == 2 and word == 'declare'
    ):
        value = 0.60
    if word.lower() == 'reply' and forum == 2:
        value = 1.04
    elif padding:
        value = 0.71
    elif text.rstrip() == '>' and hexadecimal >= 20:
        value = 0.71
    elif padded and word.startswith('",'):
        value = 0.43
    # PHP opening-tag state: 1 means '<?', 2 means '<?php' plus whitespace.
    if first:
        php = 1 if text == '<?' else 0
    elif php == 1:
        php = 2 if word == 'php' else 0
    elif php == 2 and word:
        php = 0
    forum = (2 if forum == 1 and word.lower() == 'latest' else
             1 if word.lower() == 'replies' else 0)
    is_chunk = bool(BASE64.fullmatch(text))
    has_digit = is_chunk and (has_digit or any(c.isdigit() for c in text))
    encoded = encoded + len(text) if is_chunk else 0
    hexadecimal = (
        hexadecimal + len(text) if HEX.fullmatch(text) else 0
    )
    return (doc, forum, encoded, hexadecimal, padding, php, has_digit), value

and other '一 + classifier' words (一张, 一篇, 一位, ...), and mildly negative on a bare

explains about 14% of the activation variance; the rest is small, diffuse noise on ordinary

and comma are mildly positive, especially in tool-call headers. The word
'code' is positive, especially in 'exit code'.

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

        elif first_key:

        else:

    elif token == ':':

Keep that baseline while the opening token simply repeats.  The much

smaller one marks the second ``issue`` in an issue/comment header.

        return -0.32
    if token[:1].isdigit():

    if token[:1].isalpha():

    return -0.42

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    token_id = prefix.token_ids[-1]

   closer to zero; words and punctuation are more negative.

   "Title:" header of the corpus) gets a large positive spike. Other "Title:" occurrences,
   later in a document, do not fire.
3. The tag "issue" in the "<issue_start><issue_comment>" template gets a small positive value.

Everything else is 0. The model's activation is dominated by these few rare, sharp events
plus a diffuse noise of about 0.05 everywhere, which this program does not try to model.

returns this component's predicted activation at that position.

    """Activation at the first token of a document, by what the token looks like."""
    if token.strip().isdigit():

    if token.startswith(" "):

    return -0.50

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

"""A line-ending detector, strengthened by spaced-out/tabular formatting.

Paragraph breaks, sentence punctuation, indentation and blank lines weaken it.
Interior padding (runs of spaces between fields) strengthens it. Escaped
backslash-n is a weaker line ending. Line length, digit content and non-ASCII
content provide small calibrations. Ordinary word tokens return zero.
"""

READS = ()

# Adjustments for punctuation merged into the newline's token.
ENDING_ADJUSTMENTS = (
    ('.。?!？！', -0.58),  # sentence stops
    (';', -0.40),  # semicolons
    (':：', -0.24),  # colons
    (',，', -0.08),  # commas
    ('{(', -0.68),  # opening delimiters
    ('}', -0.48),  # closing braces
    (')>', -0.19),  # parentheses and tags
    (']', 0.15),  # square brackets
    ('"\'`', -0.26),  # quotes and code quotes
    ('/\\', 0.46),  # slashes
    ('%', 1.40),  # percent signs
    ('|', 0.66),  # table bars
    ('*', -0.31),  # comment markers
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        line, previous = '', ''
    else:
        _, line, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if '\n' in token:
        head = token.split('\n', 1)[0]
        text = line + head
        ending = head.strip()[-1:]
        breaks = token.count('\n')
        value = 1.16
        value -= 0.3 * (breaks >= 2)
        value -= 0.15 * min(max(breaks - 2, 0), 3)
        for characters, adjustment in ENDING_ADJUSTMENTS:
            if ending and ending in characters:
                value += adjustment
                break
        value -= 0.16 * token.startswith(' ')
        value -= 0.2975 * min(head.count('\t'), 4)
        value -= 0.64 * ('\n' in previous)
        value -= 0.48 * (bool(previous) and previous.isspace())
        value -= 0.33 * previous.rstrip().endswith(('.', '。', '!', '?'))
        value -= 0.53 * previous.rstrip().endswith(('{', '(', '['))

        # Separate leading indentation from padding between columns.
        spaced = text.replace('\xa0', ' ')
        body = spaced.lstrip(' \t')
        indent = len(spaced) - len(body)
        runs = re.findall(r' {2,}', body)
        padding = sum(len(run) - 1 for run in runs)
        value -= 0.0045 * min(indent, 40)
        value += 0.028 * min(padding, 160)
        value += 0.07 * min(len(runs), 12)
        value -= 0.0028 * min(len(text), 200)
        length = max(1, len(text))
        value -= 0.24 * sum(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in text) / length
        value += 0.4 * sum(ch.isdigit() for ch in text) / length
        value = max(-1.0, min(5.5, value))
    elif '\\n' in token or (token == 'n' and previous.endswith('\\')):
        value = 0.55
    line = (line + token).rsplit('\n', 1)[-1][-1000:]
    return (doc, line, token), float(value)

"""A spelling-only approximation to an e-s/z/f fragment response.

Predict negative values for e followed by a new s/z/f fragment, fragments
starting with es, and continuations after es. Short consonant clusters
are stronger, especially esh and esc/esk/esq; frequent English fragments
starting with es are weaker.
Carry the last three letters through subword splits. Otherwise use zero,
or a small positive document-start offset.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(text):
    if any(unicodedata.name(c, '').startswith(('CJK', 'HANGUL')) for c in text):
        return ''
    return anyascii(text).lower()


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def es_strength(piece):
    if len(piece) <= 3 and piece.startswith('esh'):
        return -3.2
    if len(piece) <= 3 and re.match('es[ckq]', piece):
        return -2.5
    rare = zipf_frequency(piece.strip(), 'en') <= 3.5
    if rare:
        return -1.35 if len(piece) <= 3 else -0.48
    return -0.28


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    piece = spelling(text)
    continuation = not text[:1].isspace()
    value = 0.205 if first else 0.0

    if (continuation and previous.endswith('e')
            and piece[:1] in {'s', 'z', 'f'}):
        value = -1.38 if len(piece) <= 2 else -0.27
    elif piece.startswith('es'):
        value = es_strength(piece)
    elif (continuation and previous.endswith('es')
            and piece[:1].isalpha()):
        recent = previous[-3:] + piece
        clusters = list(re.finditer('e[szf][bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz]', recent))
        # A cluster ending in the new token, with at most one letter after it.
        near = bool(clusters and clusters[-1].end() >= len(recent) - 1
                    and clusters[-1].end() > len(recent) - len(piece))
        value = -1.61 if near else -0.24
    # Preserve a spelling across multiple short subword tokens, not just one.
    tail = (previous + piece) if continuation else piece
    tail = re.split('[^a-z]', tail)[-1][-3:]
    return (doc, tail), value

     letters only, same document). If not, predict 0.
  2. If the piece is one of the ending fragments -ese, -ess, -es, -se, -est, -ester, long s,

variance, mostly the large negatives; it does not reproduce the model's knowledge of which
rare word is being spelled out.

The only state is a short text tail, reset at document boundaries.

VISUAL = set('shown illustrated depicted'.split())
REPORT = set('mentioned listed stated reported presented summarized noted '
             'documented highlighted proposed suggested prescribed referenced '
             'referred'.split())
WEAK = set('indicated demonstrated explained recorded considered introduced '
           'found obtained observed used contained'.split())
REFERENCE = STRONG | VISUAL | REPORT | WEAK | {'provided', 'defined', 'given'}
LEGAL = set('required permitted prescribed determined established amended'.split())
SOURCE_NOUNS = set('teachings provisions provision requirements conditions '
                   'meaning clause definition definitions terms guidelines'.split())
PARTS = SOURCE_NOUNS | set('steps rule rules method methods examples figures '
                           'tables section sections protocol'.split())
BASE = {
    'in': .07,
    'of': .02,
    'by': .06,
    'from': .19,
    'to': 0.,
    'under': .34,
    'at': -.03,

    before = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = before + token
    word = token.strip().lower()

    prev = recent[-1] if recent else ''
    verb = prev
    if prev in {'further', 'briefly', 'above', 'below', 'here', 'extensively'}:
        verb = recent[-2] if len(recent) > 1 else ''
    if recent[-2:] == ['referred', 'to']: verb = 'referred'
    if prev == 'detail':
        earlier = recent[:-1]
        while earlier and earlier[-1] in {'in', 'more', 'greater'}: earlier.pop()

    if token.startswith(' '):

            for group, strength in ((STRONG, 6.1), (VISUAL, 4.4),

            if verb == 'given': gain = 4.6

            if verb in {'forth', 'out'} and 'set' in recent[-3:]: value += 7.8
            if verb == 'as': value += 1.4
            if verb in PARTS: value += 1.1
        if word == 'of' and verb in SOURCE_NOUNS:

        if word in {'by', 'under'}:

        if word == 'to' and prev in {'according', 'pursuant'}: value += .33

    if word in STRONG: value += .4
    if word in REFERENCE - WEAK and prev == 'as': value += .4
    if word == 'forth' and prev == 'set': value += 2.8

    # 'See' is usually a command; lower-case seeing needs a citation context.
    if word == 'see' and re.search(r'\bsee$', text, re.I):
        if token.strip() in {'See', 'SEE'}: value += 3.4
        else:

            elif re.search(r'[,;:]\s*$', before): value += 3.8

            if prev in {'i', 'we', 'you', 'they', 'can', 'could', 'will', 'to'}:

    command = re.search(
        r'(?:\bSee|[\(,;]\s*see|\bplease\s+see)\b([^.!?]{0,40})$', before)
    if command and len(command.group(1).split()) <= 3:
        if word == 'also':
            value += 7.9 + (2.5 if re.search(r'\bsee$', before) else 0.)
        if word in {'the', 'our', 'here', 'below', 'above', 'example'}: value += 1.8

    # Match whole cues even when their spelling spans several tokens.
    marker = re.search(r'\b(c\.?f|cfr|vgl|siehe|voir|vedi|veja)(\.)?$', text, re.I)
    if marker:
        name = marker[1].lower().replace('.', '')
        preceding = text[:marker.start()]
        boundary = not preceding or re.search(r'[()\[\],;:.]\s*$', preceding)
        if name == 'cf':
            if marker[2]: value += 7.7
            elif boundary: value += 5.5
        elif name in {'cfr', 'vgl'} and marker[1] != 'CFR':
            value += 4.1 if marker[2] else 10.3
        elif name in {'siehe', 'voir', 'vedi', 'veja'} and not marker[2]:
            if marker[1][0].isupper() or boundary: value += 6.8
    if re.search(r'(?:参见|详见|介绍见|请看|请参考|可以参考)$', text): value += 6.8
    if re.search(r'\be\.g(?:\.|\.,)?$', text, re.I):
        value += .4 if word in {'.', '.,'} else 1.1
        if re.search(r'\bsee\s*,?\s+e\.g', text[-35:], re.I): value += 6.5
    if re.search(r'[\(,;]\s*(?:quoting|citing)$', text): value += 4.
    if not before and token.strip() == 'Title': value = -.955
    if before == 'Title' and token.strip() == ':': value = 11.715
    return (doc, text[-160:]), value

"""A chat-format detector, strongest at the end of a message.

Tool and reasoning delimiters also activate it. The response is weaker when
very little text is available at the beginning of a document; each delimiter
has a usual strength and a short-context deficit that fades with position.
Role labels and the line breaks separating control tokens have weak echoes.
Ordinary content is assigned zero. State is just the document's token count.
"""

READS = ()

# Usual strength, short-context deficit.
DELIMITERS = {
    '<|im_end|>': (3.73, 1.94),
    '<|im_start|>': (1.91, 1.32),
    '<tool_call>': (1.28, 1.04),
    '</tool_call>': (2.18, 1.58),
    '<tool_response>': (1.09, 0.79),
    '</tool_response>': (1.67, 1.76),
    '<think>': (1.67, 2.59),
    '</think>': (1.72, 1.38),
}

LINE_BREAK_ECHO = {
    '<|im_end|>': 0.035,
    '<tool_call>': 0.085,
    '<tool_response>': 0.10,
    '<think>': 0.10,
    '</think>': 0.21,
    'assistant': 0.035,
    'user': 0.035,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    position = 0 if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if position else ''
    value = 0.0
    if token == '<|im_start|>' and not previous.endswith('\n'):
        value = 0.009  # A fresh chat header, rather than a turn transition.
    elif token in DELIMITERS:
        strength, deficit = DELIMITERS[token]
        value = max(0.0, strength - deficit / (position + 1))
    elif previous == '<|im_start|>':
        value = {'assistant': 0.107, 'user': 0.083}.get(token, 0.0)
    elif token.isspace() and '\n' in token:
        value = LINE_BREAK_ECHO.get(previous, 0.0)
    return (document, position), value

"""Chat-turn boundary detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2416.

This component fires on the special control tokens that structure a chat transcript
(Qwen's <|im_start|> / <|im_end|> turn markers and the tool-call / thinking tags), and
almost nowhere else. The strongest response is to <|im_end|>, the token that closes a
turn (about 3.7). <|im_start|> responds (about 1.9) only when it opens a new turn right
after a line break, i.e. "<|im_end|>\\n<|im_start|>"; when it directly follows
<|endoftext|> it stays silent. The tool and thinking tags respond at moderate levels
(about 1 to 2.2). Ordinary text gives roughly zero.

Everything is read from the current token and the one before it, within the same
document, so no carry is needed.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Typical activation on each control token.
MARKER_LEVEL = {
    "<|im_end|>": 3.7,        # closes a turn
    "</tool_call>": 2.15,     # closes a tool call
    "</think>": 1.7,
    "</tool_response>": 1.65,
    "<think>": 1.6,
    "<tool_call>": 1.25,
    "<tool_response>": 1.05,
}
IM_START_AFTER_NEWLINE = 1.9  # "<|im_start|>" opening a turn after "\n"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in MARKER_LEVEL:
        return carry, MARKER_LEVEL[token]
    if token == "<|im_start|>" and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1:
        same_doc = prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
        if same_doc and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "\n":
            return carry, IM_START_AFTER_NEWLINE
    return carry, 0.0

"""A short-lived response to explanatory comment openings.

English instructions, labels and relation words following comment marks get
negative values. Repeated comment decoration gets positive values. The response
uses at most eight preceding tokens and resets at document boundaries.
Line breaks usually stop it, except after block/docstring openers. Rules
also cover scaffolding words, 'instance of', and test-output labels. These are
pooled linguistic rules, not a reconstruction of token-specific responses.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

CODE = set(('bool break class console const continue cout def define echo '
    'for if import include int let namespace package print printf '
    'private protected public return string using var void while ').split())
EXAMPLES = set(('demo demonstration example examples usage ').split())
ROLES = set(('driver function helper method procedure routine ').split())
DEFINITIONS = set(('construct declare define initialise initialize instantiate ').split())
EDITS = set(('add change delete insert remove replace set update ').split())
SCAFFOLD = set(('dummy mock placeholder stub template ').split())
ASSUMPTIONS = set(('assume assumed assumes assuming hypothetical suppose supposed '
    'supposes supposing ').split())
PRONOUNS = set(('he i it she that these they this those we you your ').split())
ARTICLES = set(('a an the ').split())
AUXILIARIES = set(('are be can could is must no not should was were will would ').split())
CONJUNCTIONS = set(('and but if or unless when while ').split())
PREPOSITIONS = set(('after as at before by from in into on over with ').split())

@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def properties(s):
    w = s.strip()
    lower = w.lower()
    alpha = w.isalpha()
    verb = alpha and w.isascii() and 'verb' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(lower)
    return w, lower, alpha, bool(w and w[0].isupper()), verb


def comment_distance(history):
    for d, p in enumerate(reversed(history), 1):
        stripped = p.strip()
        block = stripped in {'/*', '/**', '<!--', '"' * 3, "'" * 3}
        marker = stripped in {'//', '///', '//!', '#', '##', '*'}
        if stripped == '*':
            end = len(history) - d
            before = ''.join(history[max(0, end - 3):end])
            marker = not before.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1].strip()
        if block or marker:
            if block or ('\n' not in p and '\\n' not in p):
                return d, .3 if stripped == '##' else 1.
            break
        if '\n' in p or '\\n' in p:
            break
    return 0, 0.


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ()
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w, lower, alpha, upper, verb = properties(s)
    value = -.1818 * (lower in SCAFFOLD)
    value += .0297 * (lower in ASSUMPTIONS)
    value -= .0724 * (lower in {'here', 'actual', 'called', 'simplicity'})
    value -= .5821 * (w == 'should' and s == w)
    value += .1495 * (s.startswith(' ') and w.startswith('*/') and '\n' not in s)
    if len(w) >= 3 and len(set(w)) == 1 and w[0] in '#*═/':
        value += .2288 * min(len(w), 16) / 16
    if lower == 'of' and history and history[-1].strip().lower() == 'instance':
        value -= .3557
    if lower == 'test' and history and history[-1].strip() == ':':
        value -= .6508 * any(p.strip() == 'PASS' for p in history[-3:])
    if lower == 'as' and history and history[-1].strip() == '*':
        value += .1072

    distance, strength = comment_distance(history)
    if distance:
        decay = strength * (1., .28, .14, .10, .07, .05, .03, .02)[distance-1]
        relation = strength * (.3, 1., .8, .5, .3, .2, .1, .05)[distance-1]
        if alpha and s[0].isspace():
            content = -.1253 - .1376 * upper - .175 * verb
            for words, weight in ((EXAMPLES, -1.3898), (ROLES, -1.1174),
                                  (DEFINITIONS, -.7312), (EDITS, -.4066),
                                  (PRONOUNS, -.6697), ({'test', 'tests'}, -1.1147)):
                content += weight * (lower in words)
            value += decay * content
            for words, weight in ((ARTICLES, -.4351), ({'of'}, -.3725),
                                  ({'to'}, -.5404), ({'for'}, -.7276),
                                  (AUXILIARIES, -.1366), (CONJUNCTIONS, -.1003),
                                  (PREPOSITIONS, -.0553)):
                value += relation * weight * (lower in words)
        elif alpha:
            value -= .0668 * decay
        value -= .231 * decay * (alpha and not w.isascii())
        value += .2211 * decay * (lower in CODE and w.islower())
        if w and set(w) <= set('/*#') and w != '*' and distance <= 3:
            value += .7822 * strength
        value += .2878 * decay * (w in {'<', '+', '{', '(', '[', '=', '>', '->'})
        value -= .2392 * relation * (w == ':')
        if len(w) >= 4 and set(w) <= {'-', '='}:
            value -= .0097 * decay
    return (doc, (history + (s,))[-8:]), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection unit 2417: the first words of a code comment.

What it does. The unit is quiet almost everywhere. Inside a comment line
(a `//`, `#`, `/*`, `--` or `<!--` earlier on the line), it turns negative on
the words that open the comment prose:

- the first word, most strongly when it is an instruction or docstring verb
  ("// Test ...", "# Add ...", "// Create ...", "# Should ...", "// Example ...");
  other capitalised first words are weakly negative, lowercase ones barely;
- the article or preposition right after a verb-led opener ("// Check *the* ...")
  is strongly negative, and other words right after the verb are mildly negative;
- the article or preposition right after a non-verb opener is mildly negative;
- later words of the comment are about zero.

A comment marker that opens a document is positive, and a marker inside an
open comment line is slightly positive. Words outside comments are zero.

The values are the average activations of these groups in the training rows,
times STRENGTH: shrunk toward zero, because the full-size values overshoot and
raise the next-token KL on held-out text.
"""

READS = ()

STRENGTH = 0.75

COMMENT_MARKS = ("//", "#", "/*", "--", "<!--", '"""', "'''")
MARKER_TOKENS = ("//", "#", "/*", "*", "///", "--", "<!--")
VERBS = set("""add create check test get set update remove delete insert make run load
save read write parse handle ensure verify print show find compute calculate generate
build init initialize open close fix move convert replace import call return returns
define use wait skip loop iterate sort filter map send pass start stop enable disable
attach extract determine store register include process prepare apply ignore reset
expected example should function implementation note assuming assume this these
simulate driver demonstrate wrap format split join count compare validate render
display trigger emit connect export fetch retrieve log debug setup""".split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = set("the a an to of for in on with and or is be it this that as if".split())

# Average activation of each group in the training rows (before STRENGTH).
DOC_MARKER = 0.57      # comment marker as the first token of a document
MARKER = 0.11          # comment marker inside an open comment line
VERB_OPENER = -0.58    # first word is an instruction/docstring verb
VERB_FUNC = -0.98      # article/preposition right after a verb opener
VERB_OTHER = -0.22     # other word right after a verb opener
CAP_OPENER = -0.14     # other capitalised first word
LOWER_OPENER = -0.06   # lowercase first word
OTHER_FUNC = -0.16     # article/preposition right after a non-verb opener
OTHER_SECOND = -0.05   # other second word
TAIL = -0.015          # later words of a comment


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[2] != doc:          # a new document resets the state
        line, words, n, verb_led = "", 0, 0, False
    else:
        line, words, n, verb_led = carry[0], carry[1], carry[3], carry[4]
    in_comment = any(m in line for m in COMMENT_MARKS)
    word = tok.strip()
    value = 0.0
    if "\n" in tok:                                # a new line: no comment yet
        line, words, verb_led = tok.split("\n")[-1], 0, False
    else:
        if word in MARKER_TOKENS:
            if n == 0:
                value = DOC_MARKER
            elif in_comment:
                value = MARKER
        elif in_comment and word.isalpha():
            is_func = word.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS
            if words == 0:                          # the opener
                verb_led = word.lower() in VERBS
                if verb_led:
                    value = VERB_OPENER
                elif word[:1].isupper():
                    value = CAP_OPENER
                else:
                    value = LOWER_OPENER
            elif words == 1:                        # the word after the opener
                if verb_led:
                    value = VERB_FUNC if is_func else VERB_OTHER
                else:
                    value = OTHER_FUNC if is_func else OTHER_SECOND
            else:
                value = TAIL
            words += 1
        line += tok
    return (line, words, doc, n + 1, verb_led), STRENGTH * value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2418 - an Italian-prose word-stem feature.

What it does, in plain terms: this unit is nearly silent except inside Italian prose. There it
reads a few word pieces, with a sign that depends on the piece:
  * a word piece ending in "z" or "zi" - the stem just before an Italian "-zione" /
    "-zioni" / "-zi-" ending (fun|z|ionario, rou|enz|ione, ra|z|ione, az|ioni): strongly positive.
    The whole ending itself ("zione", "azione", "enza") stays near zero, so the unit responds to
    a stem that is about to be completed by "-zione", not to the ending;
  * the Italian preposition " da" ("from", "by", "as"): positive;
  * the Italian words " ed", " ad", " si" (reflexive), " ecc", " ec", " ac", " oc": negative.
The same stem idea shows up in Romanian -ție words: a piece "ț" or "ţ" (prezen|ț|a) is positive
in any language.
Everywhere else (other languages, English, code, and most Italian tokens) it predicts 0.

The "Italian prose" gate is causal: a document counts as Italian once Italian function words
(di, che, della, il, per, sono, non, ...) make up at least 6% of its tokens so far, with at
least 10 tokens. The count restarts at each document boundary, as the model's attention does.
Values are the mean activation of each class inside the gate.
"""

READS = ()

ITALIAN_WORDS = {
    " di", " che", " della", " il", " per", " una", " sono", " gli", " non", " nel", " alla",
    " dei", " delle", " le", " con", " è", " e", " al", " più", " anche", " come", " questo",
    " questa", " sua", " suo", " degli", " dal", " nella", " sul", " quando", " loro", " essere",
    " molto", " ogni", " nostro", " nostri", " quello", " quella", " sulla", " dalla", " perché",
    " ancora", " dopo", " tutto", " stato", " hanno", " ma", " ci", " si", " da", " lo", " un",
}
NEG_PIECES = {" ed", " ad", " si", " ecc", " ec", " ac", " oc"}
ROMANIAN_STEMS = {"ț", "ţ"}
GATE_DENSITY = 0.06
GATE_MIN_TOKENS = 10
Z_VALUE, DA_VALUE, NEG_VALUE, RO_VALUE = 3.9, 2.7, -2.4, 2.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:          # a new document: start counting afresh
        carry = (doc, 0, 0)
    _, n, italian = carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    n, italian = n + 1, italian + (tok in ITALIAN_WORDS)
    carry = (doc, n, italian)
    piece = tok.strip().lower()
    if piece in ROMANIAN_STEMS:                    # Romanian -ție stem: any language
        return carry, RO_VALUE
    if n < GATE_MIN_TOKENS or italian < GATE_DENSITY * n:
        return carry, 0.0                          # not Italian prose: silent
    if tok in NEG_PIECES:
        return carry, NEG_VALUE
    if tok == " da":
        return carry, DA_VALUE
    if piece.endswith("z") or piece.endswith("zi"):
        return carry, Z_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2419 as a "-mat-" word-piece detector.

What the component does: it goes strongly negative on the piece of a word that completes
the letters m-a-t inside the word, the stem of Greek-derived "-matic" words:
system|atic, auto|matic, gram|matik, pragm|atics, neurofibro|mat|osis, chro|mat|ography,
and their Cyrillic and Greek forms (автомат, тематика, стоматологические, ματ).
It is most negative on the "mat", "matic" or "ematic" fragment itself, less on whole-word
tokens such as " systematic", and mildly negative on the letters that follow the stem
in the same word. The word "math" (and "Math") is weakly positive.

Why these rules: "mat" marks a stem only in some spellings. After r, i, l or x it does
not (information, format, climate, approximately, estimate stay near zero), so those
words are skipped; Cyrillic and Greek мат/ματ are counted wherever they occur.

The program follows the letters of the current word (its carry resets at each new word
and each new document), finds the last "mat" in that word, and reads how many of the
word's letters follow it, and whether they fall in this token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# "mat" not preceded by r, i, l or x; Cyrillic мат and Greek ματ are not excluded.
MAT = re.compile(r"(?<![rilx])mat|мат|ματ")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # carry: (document id, lowercase letters of the current word up to the previous token)
    word = ""
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc and token[:1].isalpha():
        word = carry[1]
    for ch in token:
        word = word + ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ""
    letters_here = sum(ch.isalpha() for ch in token)
    value = 0.0
    matches = list(MAT.finditer(word))
    if word in ("math", "maths"):
        value = 0.4
    elif matches:
        m = matches[-1]
        after = len(word) - m.end()  # letters of the word after its last "mat"
        inside = after < letters_here  # the "mat" ends inside this token
        spaced = token[:1] == " "  # a whole-word token, such as " systematic"
        if inside and after == 0:
            value = -2.5 if spaced else -4.0  # the stem's "mat" completes here
        elif inside and after == 1:
            value = 0.4  # "math": the letter after the stem
        elif inside and after == 2 and not spaced:
            value = -2.8  # "matic" in one piece
        else:
            value = -0.3  # later letters of a word with a stem
    return (doc, word), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2421 -- a "path and dotted-name segment" detector (negative).

This component writes a negative value into the residual stream whenever the model is
reading a file path, URL, domain or dotted/hyphenated identifier, and is strongest on the
separator that opens a new segment of it:

- "/" opening a directory or file name in a path, e.g. "/test", "/workspace", "/src"
  (about -2.2; single letters such as "/s" or "/c" only about -1).
- "." opening a name, e.g. the ".com" of github.com or ".git" (about -1; -2 for common
  domain and repo endings like com, org, git).
- A segment that opens a line, as in a listing of paths, is stronger by about 1.
- Inside a longer technical word (no space since its start), a joining "-" or "_" weighs
  about -0.7 and any other non-letter piece about -0.3.
- Ordinary words, spaces, digits and punctuation in prose are 0.

word or line; no state is carried between positions.

READS = ()

import re

DOMAIN_OR_REPO_ENDINGS = {"com", "org", "net", "edu", "gov", "git", "io"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    if not re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", cur):

    name = cur[1:]

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 2422: a code-delimiter detector with document-opening spikes.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Mostly near zero. It is a weak, positive response to tokens that close or open code
  delimiters: a closing quote that ends a string (about +0.25), a closing bracket such as
  ) ] } (about +0.1), a "[" (about +0.2).
- A "<" that opens a header or tag gets a strong response: +1.9 right after "#include",
  about +1.0 after indentation (start of a line), and +0.15 for any other "<" (comparisons).
- A heredoc marker "EOF" gets +0.8.
- A run of middle-dot filler tokens "··" gets -0.35.
- Rare document openings give very large values: a document that starts "Title:" gives
  +12.2 on the colon, a document that starts "#include <" gives +2.3 on the "<", and a
  document opening with a run of carriage returns gives +7.9 on the first five tokens.
- Everything else predicts 0.

first tokens of each packed document.

READS = ()

# Document openings: the first two tokens of a document, and the value on the second.
OPENING_PAIRS = {("Title", ":"): 12.2, ("#include", " <"): 2.3}
CR_RUN_VALUE = 7.86     # a document that opens with carriage returns, first five tokens
HEREDOC_EOF = 0.8
FILLER_DOTS = "··"      # the middle-dot filler token
FILLER_VALUE = -0.35


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "head": [], "n": 0, "all_cr": True}
    carry["n"] += 1
    carry["all_cr"] = carry["all_cr"] and tok == "\r"
    if len(carry["head"]) < 2:
        carry["head"].append(tok)

    # Document openings.
    if carry["all_cr"] and carry["n"] <= 5:
        return carry, CR_RUN_VALUE
    if carry["n"] == 2 and tuple(carry["head"]) in OPENING_PAIRS:
        return carry, OPENING_PAIRS[tuple(carry["head"])]

    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 else ""
    if tok == FILLER_DOTS:
        return carry, FILLER_VALUE
    if tok == "EOF":
        return carry, HEREDOC_EOF
    if tok in (" <", "<"):
        if prev == "#include":
            return carry, 1.9
        if prev.strip() == "" and prev != "":   # after indentation
            return carry, 1.0
        return carry, 0.15

    # Closing delimiters. Quote parity on the current line tells a closing quote from an opening one.
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[-2] if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 else ""
    line = before.split("\n")[-1]

            return carry, 0.25
        return carry, 0.05
    if tok in (" [", "["):
        return carry, 0.2
    if tok in (")", "]", "}", "()", "')", "']", '")', '"]'):
        return carry, 0.1
    return carry, 0.0

"a section") stays near zero. Item nouns (point, row, column, part, position, ...) fire only
after a reference cue ("at point", "from row"). The period or suffix that completes an
abbreviation ("Fig.", "FIGS", "Eqs") fires too, a bit less than the label itself.

token, and predicts a fixed value per position. No state is carried between positions.
"""

          "Sections", "Sect", "Sec", "section", "Eq", "Eqs", "Eqn", "Equation", "Article", "Step",
          "Algorithm", "Chapter", "§", "Appendix", "Proposition", "Lemma", "Example", "Rule",
          "subsection", "subparagraph", "paragraph", "Verse", "verse", "Case", "Line", "Lines"}
# Abbreviations that are often followed by a period ("Fig. 3") or a plural suffix ("FIGS").
ABBREVIATIONS = {"FIG", "FIGS", "Fig", "Figs", "Eq", "Eqs", "Eqn", "Sec", "Sect"}
# Pieces a label can be split into, and the period that follows an abbreviation.
CONTINUATIONS = {".", "S", "s", "igs", "qs", "ures", "ation"}
# Nouns that name an item only when used as a reference ("at point", "from row").
ITEM_NOUNS = {"point", "row", "column", "part", "position", "angle", "group", "line", "step",
              "page", "day"}
# Words that introduce a reference.
CUES = {"in", "see", "See", "at", "from", "of", "to", "under", "by", "shown", "illustrated",
        "In", "At", "From", "with", "on", "cf", "Referring", "and", "(", "["}

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 2427.

What it does: a word detector with a negative sign. It goes strongly negative on
the token for "loan" (English loan(s), Chinese 贷 / 贷款 / 借款), on the Chinese
person nouns 男 (man) and 女 (woman) and a few compounds of them (男子, 女子, 男生,
女生, 女孩), on the award characters 奖 and 獎, and on 款 (payment / fund). Other
tokens that merely contain 男, 女, 奖 or 款 (女性, 男友, 奖励, 这款 ...) get a weak
value, and every other token is 0.

Why: this component's output is almost entirely carried by these words, so a
word list captures most of its variance and, put into the model, most of its effect.
What the simple version gets: variance explained about 0.30 and about 72% of the
end-to-end KL of switching the component off. What it leaves out: the many small
values on ordinary tokens, and the positive spikes on "�" fragments of multi-byte
characters in Japanese, Korean and Chinese text, which have no simple rule.
"""

READS = ()

LOAN = {"loan", "loans"}                                   # English loan(s)
CHINESE_LOAN = {"贷", "贷款", "借款"}                       # Chinese for loan / credit
GENDER = {"男": -3.9, "女": -2.9, "男子": -2.5, "女子": -2.3,
          "男生": -3.0, "女生": -1.9, "女孩": -1.8}         # man / woman and compounds
AWARD = {"奖": -4.3, "獎": -5.7}                           # award / prize
COMPOUND_CHARS = ("男", "女", "奖", "款")                   # weak value if merely contained


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in LOAN or word in CHINESE_LOAN:
        return None, -4.0
    if word in GENDER:
        return None, GENDER[word]
    if word in AWARD:
        return None, AWARD[word]
    if word == "款":
        return None, -2.2
    if any(c in word for c in COMPOUND_CHARS):
        return None, -0.8
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 2429: a sparse word detector.

It is silent almost everywhere. It goes negative on the verb "happen" (happen,
happens, happened, happening) and on "chance". Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

NEG = -3.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word.startswith("happen") or word.startswith("chance"):
        value = NEG
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2430: a "first token of a document" feature.

What it does: the component is silent almost everywhere. Its activation is large only at
the first token of a document (or of a packed row, where the model also sees nothing
before it). A first token has no earlier context, so the component's value there is a
fixed function of the token's spelling. Roughly:

  - a capitalised word after a space (" Test", " Power", " Network": a word that
    would normally sit mid-sentence) gives a large positive value;
  - most other word starts give a moderate negative value: a lowercase word after a
    space, a capitalised word with no space ("When", "Two"), a lowercase or CJK word
    with no space;
  - punctuation and whitespace starts are near zero.

Every other position predicts 0; there the activation is small noise (std about 0.05).

The numbers are group means over the vocabulary, measured on training text. Splitting
first tokens into these few classes explains about 73% of the variance of the activation
on training text. A full per-token table would explain about 95%, but it has no concept
behind it, so this program uses the classes instead.
"""

READS = ()

# Values by class of the first token (group means measured on training data).
MID_SENTENCE_CAPITAL = 6.0  # " Test", " Power"
SPACED_LOWER = -3.1  # " significantly", " profound"
UNSPACED_CAPITAL = -4.5  # "When", "Two": capital letter, no leading space
UNSPACED_ALL_CAPS = -2.4  # "THE", "NASA"
UNSPACED_LOWER = -2.1  # "the", "ing"
NON_LATIN_LETTER = -3.2  # CJK or other non-ASCII letters with no space
NON_LATIN_SPACED = -1.0  # the same with a leading space
PUNCTUATION = -2.1  # punctuation, digits, newline (no space)
SPACED_PUNCTUATION = -0.7  # punctuation, digits with a leading space


def first_token_value(token: str) -> float:
    """The component's activation for a token that is the first of its document."""
    spaced = token[:1] == " "
    core = token.lstrip(" ")
    head = core[:1]
    if not head:
        return 0.0
    if head.isascii() and head.isalpha():
        if head.isupper():
            if spaced:
                return MID_SENTENCE_CAPITAL
            if len(core) > 1 and core.isupper():
                return UNSPACED_ALL_CAPS
            return UNSPACED_CAPITAL
        return SPACED_LOWER if spaced else UNSPACED_LOWER
    if head.isalpha():
        return NON_LATIN_SPACED if spaced else NON_LATIN_LETTER
    return SPACED_PUNCTUATION if spaced else PUNCTUATION


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component at the newest token: nonzero only if it starts a document
    (or the packed row)."""
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, float(first_token_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""Approximate research-methods and scholarly-boilerplate signal.

Recent study/laboratory vocabulary strengthens negative predictions for descriptions
of procedures, participants, constraints, and approvals. Local grammar, headings,
and citation conventions add smaller corrections. This is a coarse word-class
account, not an exact predictor of every word's context-dependent activation.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
READS = ()

CLASSES = {
    'study': 'study experiment research trial survey',
    'technical_description': 'data dataset experimental schematic drawings',
    'gratitude': (
        'thank thanks grateful acknowledge acknowledged acknowledgements '
        'acknowledgments acknowledgement acknowledgment'
    ),
    'ethics': (
        'ethics ethical consent eligibility eligible inclusion exclusion recruitment '
        'approval approved'
    ),
    'lab_material': 'strain antibody plasmid apparatus',
    'participation': (
        'participate participated involved collected selected excluded recruited '
        'sacrificed included searched'
    ),
    'procedure': (
        'procedure protocol methodology setup preparation collection sampling '
        'isolation implementation identification generation notation selection '
        'extraction sequencing statistics statistical'
    ),
    'method': (
        'method approach technique algorithm model process design analysis assessment '
        'evaluation calculation'
    ),
    'population': (
        'sample participant patient subject respondent cohort specimen animal dataset '
        'material'
    ),
    'property': (
        'variable parameter condition size period input output system code character '
        'objective safety'
    ),
    'constraint': 'criterion criteria requirement limitation validity reliability relevant',
    'paper': 'author manuscript funding declaration conflict',
    'past': 'was',
    'plural_past': 'were',
    'used': 'used',
    'use': 'use uses using choose chose chosen',
    'author_action': (
        'denote denotes define defines consider assume examine describe investigate '
        'employ'
    ),
    'evidence': (
        'shown show illustrated noted reported described proposed demonstrated '
        'revealed depicted referenced seen found'
    ),
    'demonstrative': 'this these our we',
}
LEXICON = {w: c for c, words in CLASSES.items() for w in words.split()}
TOPIC = set((
    'analysis antibodies antibody approval assay assays bacteria bacterial blot '
    'buffer buffers cdna cell cells clinical cohort consent culture cultured '
    'cultures dataset datasets dna enzyme enzymes ethical ethics exclusion '
    'experiment experimental experiments gene genes genome genomes inclusion '
    'manuscript measured membrane membranes method methodology methods mice mouse '
    'mrna nucleotide nucleotides participant participants patient patients pcr '
    'plasma primer primers procedure protein proteins protocol rabbit rabbits '
    'randomized rat rats reagent reagents recruitment regression research rna '
    'sample samples sampling serum solution solutions specimens statistical '
    'strain strains studies study subjects tissue tissues trial trials'
).split())

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def classify(token):
    w = token.strip().lower()
    group = LEXICON.get(w)
    if w.startswith('acknowled'):
        group = 'gratitude'
    if not group and w.endswith('s'):
        group = LEXICON.get(w[:-1])
    if not group and w.endswith('ies'):
        group = LEXICON.get(w[:-3]+'y')
    return w, group or 'other', w in TOPIC


# Columns: base, topic, determiner, author, preceding research word,
# capitalized, line start, prepositional complement, plural, preceding pronoun.
COEFFICIENTS = {
    'study': (0, -0.24, -0.48, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'technical_description': (0, -0.27, -0.24, 0, 0.26, 0, 0, 0, -0.67, 0),
    'gratitude': (-0.27, -1.26, 0, -0.76, 0, 0, 0.22, 0, 0, 0),
    'ethics': (-0.27, -2.67, 0, 0, -0.74, 0, 0.23, 0.28, -0.33, 0),
    'lab_material': (-0.39, -0.68, 0, 0, 0.25, -0.22, 0, 0.37, -0.24, 0),
    'participation': (0, -1.65, 0, -0.83, 0, 0.26, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'procedure': (0, -1.02, 0, 0, -1.43, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'method': (0, -0.26, 0, 0, -0.55, 0, -0.24, 0, 0, 0),
    'population': (0, -0.45, 0, 0, -0.91, 0, -0.28, 0, 0, 0),
    'property': (0, -0.29, 0, 0, -0.35, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'constraint': (-0.29, -1.15, 0, 0, -1.36, 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'paper': (0, -0.85, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'past': (0, -1.13, 0, 0, -0.6, 0.21, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'plural_past': (-0.36, -1.43, 0.53, 0, -0.86, 0.45, 0.25, 0, 0, 0.29),
    'used': (-0.35, -1.42, 0, -0.57, -0.84, -0.31, 0.34, 0, 0, 0.34),
    'use': (0, -0.25, 0, -0.59, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'author_action': (0, 0, 0, -0.26, -0.22, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'evidence': (0, 0.34, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    'demonstrative': (0, -0.2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token, doc = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = doc, 0., '', '', '', ''
    _, topic, prev, prev2, line, tail = carry
    joined = tail + token if token and token[0].isalpha() else token
    w, group, marker = classify(joined)
    if len(w) > 35:
        w, group, marker = classify(token)
    science = min(topic / 4., 1.)
    pronoun = prev in {'he', 'she', 'it', 'they', 'there', 'that', 'which', 'i', 'who'}
    related = classify(prev)[1] in {
        'study', 'procedure', 'method', 'population', 'property', 'technical_description',
        'ethics', 'lab_material', 'constraint'}
    x = (
        1., 0. if pronoun and group in {'past', 'plural_past'} else science,
        prev in {'the', 'this', 'these', 'our', 'their', 'a', 'an'},
        prev in {'we', 'i'}, related,
        bool(token.strip() and token.strip()[0].isupper()), not line.strip(),
        prev in {'of', 'in', 'for', 'with', 'from'},
        w.endswith('s') and group not in {
            'past', 'plural_past', 'present', 'use', 'used', 'evidence',
            'demonstrative', 'author_action', 'participation'},
        pronoun and group in {'past', 'plural_past', 'present', 'use', 'used'},
    )
    value = sum(a*b for a,b in zip(COEFFICIENTS.get(group, ()), x))
    # Attribution and citation cues point in the other direction.
    value += {'by': .24, 'from': -.28}.get(w, 0.) * science
    if '\n' in token:
        heading = (1 <= len(line.split()) <= 12 and len(line) < 110
                   and not any(c in line for c in '.!?;{}='))
        value -= .34 * science * heading
    value += .31 * (w == 'example' and prev == 'for')
    value += .27 * (w == 'al' and prev == 'et')
    value += .51 * (prev == '](' and token == '#')
    value -= .58 * (w == '-type' and prev == 'ref')
    value += .71 * (w == 'by' and prev in {'study', 'studies', 'paper', 'work'})
    value -= 3.35 * (w == 'by' and prev == 'approved')
    value -= 1.24 * (w == 'interest' and prev == 'of' and prev2 == 'conflict')
    value -= 1.22 * (w == 'to' and prev == 'grateful')
    value -= 1.04 * (w in {
        'acknowledgments', 'acknowledgements', 'acknowledgement'})
    topic = topic * .99 + marker
    line = (line + token)[-120:].rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    tail = joined.rsplit(None, 1)[-1] if joined and joined[-1].isalpha() else ''
    return (doc, topic, w, prev, line, tail), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2431 as a "research-methods register" detector.

What the component does: its activation is near zero in most text, but goes clearly
negative inside the Methods / Participants / Ethics passages of scientific papers.
The strongest negatives are on research-ethics and participant words ("informed
consent", "ethical approval", "inclusion criteria", "participants", "recruited",
"excluded"), on the study-procedure word "study", and on the passive auxiliaries
that say what was done to the material: "Data were", "All samples were", "the
survey was used", "the study was approved". The same auxiliaries after a pronoun
("they were", "it was") stay near zero. Reporting verbs such as "reported",
"described", "proposed" push it slightly positive. The negative values grow the
longer the text has stayed in this register.

What this program does, per token:
  1. Keeps a running "methods density" D: each token it multiplies D by 0.985 and adds
     1 if the token is a strong or study-procedure word or was/were/used. D resets at
     each document start.
  2. Scores the current token from the lexicon below, using D:
       strong methods word          -> -0.10 - 0.44 * D
       study-procedure word         -> -0.01 - 0.08 * D
       was / were / used after a noun
                                    -> -0.18 - 0.22 * D
       was / were / used otherwise  -> -0.08 - 0.07 * D
       reporting verb               ->  0.07 + 0.07 * D
       anything else                ->  0
  The prediction uses only the current token and the text before it, so it is causal.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DECAY = 0.985

# Research-ethics, participant and selection vocabulary: the strongest negative words.
STRONG = frozenset(
    """consent criteria ethics ethical approval approvals approved approve inclusion
    exclusion excluded selection recruitment recruited participants participant
    participated participate enrolled protocol protocols availability limitations
    limitation sacrificed""".split()
)

# Study-procedure nouns and verbs of methods sections.
PROCEDURE = frozenset(
    """study studies animals animal strains strain collection collected selected
    extraction extracted procedures procedure data datasets samples sample analysis
    analyses survey questionnaire antibodies antibody preparation cohort manuscript
    methods methodology authors searched included chosen chose instrument apparatus
    cells mice patients subjects""".split()
)

# The passive / past-tense auxiliaries that report what was done.
AUXILIARY = frozenset("was were used".split())

# Verbs that report results or cite earlier work: mildly positive.
REPORTING = frozenset(
    """reported described proposed suggested indicated demonstrated found shown noted
    mentioned discussed illustrated refer refers previously""".split()
)

# Words that are not nouns: a subject like "they", "it" or "there" before "were" or "was".
PRONOUNS = frozenset(
    """they we you it there i he she who which that and but or also not this these
    those then so""".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """One position: the activation predicted from this token, the word before it and
    the methods density of the text so far. carry = (density, document id of the last
    token)."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[1] != doc:
        density = 0.0  # a new document starts a new register
        previous = ""
    else:
        density = carry[0]
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    noun_before = previous.isalpha() and len(previous) > 1 and previous.lower() not in PRONOUNS

    hit = 0.0
    if word in STRONG:
        value = -0.10 - 0.44 * density
        hit = 1.0
    elif word in AUXILIARY:
        if noun_before:
            value = -0.18 - 0.22 * density
        else:
            value = -0.08 - 0.07 * density
        hit = 1.0
    elif word in PROCEDURE:
        value = -0.01 - 0.08 * density
        hit = 1.0
    elif word in REPORTING:
        value = 0.07 + 0.07 * density
    else:
        value = 0.0

    return (DECAY * density + hit, doc), float(value)
